studyQA.question: What is Agent Development Kit (ADK)?
studyQA.answer: An open-source, model-agnostic framework for building, debugging and deploying agents in code. It offers template workflows such as sequential, loop and parallel.

studyQA.question: What is Agent Platform Sessions?
studyQA.answer: Stores the individual interactions between users and agents, so a conversation keeps its history. Memory Bank draws its long-term memories from stored sessions.

studyQA.question: What is Agent Platform Memory Bank?
studyQA.answer: Generates long-term memories dynamically from conversations between a user and an agent, so the agent can recall them in later sessions. Formerly called Vertex AI Agent Engine Memory Bank.

studyQA.question: What is Model Garden?
studyQA.answer: A catalogue of Google's frontier models such as Gemini, plus third-party and open-source models.

studyQA.question: What is Skill Registry?
studyQA.answer: A secure, private repository on Agent Platform that stores skills as self-contained packages.

topics.title: 3.2 Integrating enterprise domain knowledge

studyQA.question: What is Vector Search?

studyQA.question: What is RAG Engine?
studyQA.answer: A component of Agent Platform that facilitates retrieval-augmented generation: it connects private enterprise data to LLMs to improve answer accuracy and reduce hallucinations.

studyQA.question: What is Agent Identity?
studyQA.answer: Gives each agent a fully managed, unique identity, so access to resources can be controlled and audited per agent.

studyQA.question: What is Agent Registry?
studyQA.answer: A centralized catalog for discovering, tracking and managing agents, tools and MCP servers across the organization.

studyQA.question: What is Agent Identity?
studyQA.answer: Gives each agent a fully managed, unique identity, so access to resources can be controlled and audited per agent.

studyQA.question: What is Agent Gateway?
studyQA.answer: The governance and security enforcement layer for agents: a central policy enforcement point for agent tool calls, authentication and security policies. It is the networking component of Agent Platform.

studyQA.question: What is Client-to-Agent?
studyQA.answer: An Agent Gateway mode for inbound traffic: it secures communications between clients and the agents or MCP tools they reach.

studyQA.question: What is Agent-to-Anywhere?
studyQA.answer: An Agent Gateway mode for outbound traffic: it governs requests that agents send to external tools and services.

studyQA.question: What is Agent Registry?
studyQA.answer: A centralized catalog for discovering, tracking and managing agents, tools and MCP servers across the organization.

studyQA.question: What is Model Armor?
studyQA.answer: A Google Cloud service that screens prompts and model responses for harmful content, prompt injection and jailbreaks, sensitive data and malicious links.

questions.question: A team wants business analysts to build and turn on a chat agent in the Gemini Enterprise web app without writing code. Which tool fits?
questions.explanation: Workflow Builder is an interactive no-code, low-code platform for creating, managing and turning on chat agents and workflows in the Gemini Enterprise web app.
whyOthersWrong: ADK is an open-source framework for building agents in code, so it does not suit analysts who will not write code.
Agents CLI is a command-line tool for building, evaluating and deploying agents, not a no-code builder.
Agent Runtime runs and scales deployed agents; it is not where a no-code agent is built.

questions.question: A support flow has fixed stages. The agent must move between pages, follow transition routes and react to events. Which design matches?
options: A state-based workflow with pages, transition routes and event handlers
A single long system prompt with no states
A vector index of past conversations
questions.explanation: State-based workflows model a flow as pages joined by transition routes, with event handlers for what happens along the way, which suits fixed stages.
whyOthersWrong: A prompt alone does not give the explicit stages and transitions the flow needs.
A vector index retrieves knowledge; it does not define the stages of a flow.
A coding agent writes and runs code; it is not a way to model a staged support flow.

questions.question: An agent must answer from the company's proprietary documents. A managed Google feature already connects and searches such data. What should the architect do first?
options: Build a custom ingestion and search pipeline
Fine-tune a model on the documents before anything else
Copy the documents into the system prompt
Connect the data through Gemini Enterprise and Agent Search
questions.explanation: The exam favours the managed, native feature when it meets the requirement. Gemini Enterprise and Agent Search connect to and query enterprise data.
whyOthersWrong: A custom pipeline is more to build and run when a managed feature already meets the need.
Fine-tuning is not the first step when a managed connection to the data exists.
A prompt holds limited text and cannot stand in for connecting and querying the document set.

questions.question: A coding agent will run generated code. Security requires that it can touch only a limited environment while it edits and runs code. What should be used?
options: Run it directly on a developer laptop with admin rights
Give it the production project's owner role
A secure sandbox such as Cloud Workstations or Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE)
Disable code execution and have it only suggest text
questions.explanation: Coding agents should run in secure sandboxes, for example GKE, Cloud Workstations or Antigravity, which limit what the agent can touch.
whyOthersWrong: A laptop with admin rights does not limit what the agent can touch.
The owner role gives broad access, the opposite of a limit.
Disabling execution removes the capability the team wants instead of making it safe.

questions.question: A coding agent needs access to the team's internal tools and a reusable set of instructions. Which two things configure that?
options: Principal access boundary policies and Model Armor
Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and custom skills
Agent Gateway modes and Agent Registry
questions.explanation: Coding agents are configured with MCP servers, custom skills and access to tools.
whyOthersWrong: Those are governance and screening controls, not how a coding agent gets tools and instructions.
Those govern and catalogue agent traffic; they do not give a coding agent its tools.
Those store conversation state and memories, not tools or skills.

questions.question: A team wants one command-line tool to build, evaluate and deploy agents on Google Cloud, with a skills package for coding agents. What is it?
questions.explanation: Agents CLI is a command-line tool and skills package for building, evaluating and deploying AI agents on Google Cloud.
whyOthersWrong: Workflow Builder is a no-code builder in the Gemini Enterprise web app.
Model Garden is a catalogue of models, not a build and deploy tool.
Skill Registry stores skills as packages; it does not build or deploy agents.

questions.question: In Antigravity, which list names the ways to customise a coding agent for enterprise workflows?
options: Skills, plugins, extension hooks, rules and subagents
questions.explanation: Antigravity is customised with skills, plugins, extension hooks, rules and subagents.
whyOthersWrong: Pages and routes belong to state-based low-code workflows.
Those are memory and retrieval parts, not coding-agent customisation.
Those are governance and traffic terms, not extension points.

questions.question: A developer wants an open-source, model-agnostic framework to build and debug agents in code, with sequential, loop and parallel template workflows. Which fits?
questions.explanation: ADK is an open-source, model-agnostic framework for building, debugging and deploying agents in code, with sequential, loop and parallel workflow templates.
whyOthersWrong: Workflow Builder is no-code or low-code, not a code framework.
Model Armor screens prompts and responses; it does not build agents.
Agent Gateway enforces policy on traffic; it does not build agents.

questions.question: An agent must remember a conversation's history within that conversation. Which component stores the individual interactions between a user and the agent?
questions.explanation: Sessions store the individual interactions between users and agents, so a conversation keeps its history.
whyOthersWrong: Memory Bank generates long-term memories for later sessions; it is not the conversation history.
Model Garden is a catalogue of models.
Agent Registry is a catalogue of agents, tools and MCP servers.

questions.question: A returning customer should find that the agent recalls their preferences from earlier conversations. Which component generates and keeps such long-term memories?
questions.explanation: Memory Bank generates long-term memories dynamically from conversations, so the agent can recall them in later sessions.
whyOthersWrong: Sessions keep the history of a conversation; the long-term memories come from Memory Bank, which draws on stored sessions.
Agent Gateway enforces policy on agent traffic.
Cloud Trace shows where latency comes from; it stores no memories.

questions.question: An architect needs one place to choose among Google's frontier models such as Gemini, plus third-party and open-source models. Where?
questions.explanation: Model Garden is a catalogue of Google's frontier models such as Gemini, plus third-party and open-source models.
whyOthersWrong: Skill Registry stores skills, not models.
Agent Registry catalogues agents, tools and MCP servers.
RAG Engine connects private data to language models; it is not a model catalogue.

questions.question: An organisation wants a secure, private repository on Agent Platform where agent skills are stored as self-contained packages. Which?
questions.explanation: Skill Registry is a secure, private repository on Agent Platform that stores skills as self-contained packages.
whyOthersWrong: Agent Registry catalogues agents, tools and MCP servers, not skill packages.
Model Garden catalogues models.
Agent Identity gives each agent a unique identity for access control.

questions.question: An agent must reduce hallucinations by grounding answers in private enterprise data. Which Agent Platform component connects that data to language models for retrieval-augmented generation?
questions.explanation: RAG Engine facilitates retrieval-augmented generation by connecting private enterprise data to language models, improving accuracy and reducing hallucinations.
whyOthersWrong: Model Armor screens content for harm, injection and sensitive data; it does not ground answers.
Agent Gateway enforces policy on agent traffic.
Agents CLI builds, evaluates and deploys agents.

questions.question: Each agent must have its own managed identity so access to resources can be controlled and audited per agent, not through a shared account. What gives that?
options: A shared service account for every agent
questions.explanation: Agent Identity gives each agent a fully managed, unique identity, so access can be controlled and audited per agent.
whyOthersWrong: A shared account cannot tell the agents apart, so access cannot be controlled or audited per agent.
Agent Registry catalogues agents; it does not give them identities.
Model Garden catalogues models.

questions.question: The organisation wants a central catalogue for discovering, tracking and managing agents, tools and MCP servers. Which?
questions.explanation: Agent Registry is a centralised catalogue for discovering, tracking and managing agents, tools and MCP servers across the organisation.
whyOthersWrong: Skill Registry stores skills, not agents and MCP servers.
Vector Search stores and searches data for AI applications.
Cloud Logging records logs; it is not a catalogue of agents.

questions.question: Two agents built by different teams must work together. Which open protocol lets an agent reach tools, and which lets agents coordinate with each other?
options: A2A for tools and MCP between agents
MCP for tools and Agent2Agent (A2A) between agents
questions.explanation: Agents are orchestrated with agentic protocols such as MCP and Agent2Agent (A2A). MCP connects an agent to tools; A2A connects agents to one another.
whyOthersWrong: That swaps the two protocols' roles.
OAuth 2.0 authenticates calls; it is not a protocol for tools or agent-to-agent coordination.
Model Armor screens content; it is not an orchestration protocol.

questions.question: A task's steps depend on one another and must run in order, each using the previous result. Which workflow shape fits?
options: A loop with no exit condition
questions.explanation: Pick the workflow shape from the task's dependencies. Steps that depend on earlier results run in sequence.
whyOthersWrong: Parallel agents suit independent work, not steps that need earlier results.
A loop with no exit condition would never finish.
Without a handoff the later steps cannot use the earlier results.

questions.question: Which service is the high-performance, scalable environment for deploying, operating and scaling agents, formerly called Agent Engine?
questions.explanation: Agent Runtime is the scalable runtime environment for deploying, operating and scaling agents. It was formerly called Agent Engine.
whyOthersWrong: Agent Registry catalogues agents.
Agent Gateway enforces policy on agent traffic.
Model Garden catalogues models.

questions.question: Before release, the team wants to judge an agent's answers and its tool calls against known-good examples. What should they build?
options: A single manual test of one happy path
A vector index of the production logs
A golden dataset of prompts and edge cases to evaluate against
questions.explanation: Evaluation uses test sets such as golden data, prompts and edge cases, and assesses the agent's tool execution against success criteria.
whyOthersWrong: One happy path misses edge cases and the tool calls.
A vector index retrieves data; it does not evaluate the agent.
A longer prompt changes behaviour but does not measure it.

questions.question: An agent passed evaluation once. How should the team keep its quality known as it changes in production?
options: Rely on users to report problems
Run continuous evaluation, including online evaluation of live traffic
Evaluate only the final text, never the tool calls
questions.explanation: Agent evaluation is continuous: multi-turn autoraters and online evaluation of live traffic assess quality over time, and tool execution is assessed too.
whyOthersWrong: A single evaluation goes stale as the agent and its data change.
Waiting for reports means problems are found late.
Tool calls are part of what the evaluation assesses, so skipping them leaves a gap.

questions.question: A team must choose where to deploy an agent. Which are the runtimes the exam guide names for this choice?
options: Model Armor, Agent Gateway and Agent Registry
Agent Runtime, Cloud Run and GKE
Workflow Builder, ADK and Agents CLI
Cloud Trace, Cloud Logging and Vector Search
questions.explanation: The deployment runtime is chosen by use case, requirements and cost from Agent Runtime, Cloud Run and GKE.
whyOthersWrong: Those are security and governance parts, not runtimes.
Those are build tools, not where an agent runs.
Those are observability and data parts, not runtimes.

questions.question: A deployed agent is slow and sometimes loops on its reasoning. Which Google Cloud tools show where the latency and the loop come from?
questions.explanation: Troubleshooting agents uses Cloud Trace and Cloud Logging to find where latency or a reasoning loop comes from.
whyOthersWrong: Model Armor screens content and Agent Registry catalogues agents; neither traces latency.
Those are catalogues and do not show runtime behaviour.
Those build agents; they do not diagnose a running one.

questions.question: Security wants one governance and enforcement layer for agent tool calls, authentication and security policies. Which Agent Platform component is it?
questions.explanation: Agent Gateway is the governance and security enforcement layer for agents, a central policy enforcement point for tool calls, authentication and security policies.
whyOthersWrong: Agent Registry catalogues agents; it does not enforce policy on traffic.
Model Garden catalogues models.
Sessions store conversation history.

questions.question: An agent sends requests to external tools and services. Which Agent Gateway mode governs that outbound traffic?
questions.explanation: Agent-to-Anywhere governs requests that agents send to external tools and services. Client-to-Agent secures inbound traffic.
whyOthersWrong: Client-to-Agent secures inbound communications between clients and agents, not outbound requests.
Agent Identity gives each agent a unique identity; it is not a traffic mode.
Model Armor screens content; it is not a traffic mode.

questions.question: Prompts and replies must be screened for prompt injection, jailbreaks, sensitive data and malicious links. Which service does this?
questions.explanation: Model Armor screens prompts and model responses for harmful content, prompt injection and jailbreaks, sensitive data and malicious links.
whyOthersWrong: Agent Identity identifies the agent; it does not screen content.
Agent Registry catalogues agents.
Cloud Trace shows latency, not content problems.

questions.question: An agent can take an action with serious consequences, such as paying a large invoice. Which safeguard fits?
options: A human-in-the-loop approval step before the action
Let the agent act, then review the logs next month
Give the agent broader permissions so it is never blocked
Remove the guardrails to reduce latency
questions.explanation: Safety frameworks combine guardrails with human-in-the-loop (HITL) approval where risk requires it.
whyOthersWrong: Reviewing later cannot undo a harmful action that has already happened.
Broader permissions increase risk, the opposite of a safeguard.
Removing guardrails makes risky actions easier.

questions.question: A company's support knowledge sits in recorded calls, screen videos and product photos. The agent must use it. What does the exam guide expect the architect to configure?

Ingestion that processes unstructured multimodal data such as video, audio and images

questions.question: Which tool does the exam guide say augments Antigravity to build, scale, govern and optimise deployed agents?

Cloud Trace and Cloud Logging are observability tools.
Agent Identity and Agent Registry are security and governance tools.

questions.question: A multiagent system needs each agent to have its own identity, be found in a catalogue, run in a managed environment and obey policies. Which tools does the exam guide pair for this?

questions.question: What should a continuous evaluation pipeline assess, against established success criteria?

The number of Skill Registry entries
The size of the Model Garden catalogue

The catalogue size is not a measure of the agent's behaviour.

questions.question: Operations wants to monitor and optimise agents for performance, reliability and cost. Which three problems does the exam guide say to identify?

Logic errors, latency bottlenecks and hallucinations
Inbound mode, outbound mode and identity

Cloud Trace tracks request latency.

whyOthersWrong: Principal access boundary policies limit what an identity can reach.

Reranking reorders retrieved results.

whyOthersWrong: BigQuery is a data platform.
Cloud Storage is object storage.

questions.question: An analyst needs a fully managed, serverless, AI-ready data platform to analyse data with SQL and Python. Which service fits?

Cloud Storage is object storage.

questions.question: Which service gives scalable, managed object storage for any amount of data?
questions.explanation: Cloud Storage is a scalable, managed object storage service for storing and retrieving any amount of data at any time.
whyOthersWrong: Cloud SQL stores relational rows, not objects.

whyOthersWrong: Cloud SQL is a relational database service.

Cloud Storage is object storage.

whyOthersWrong: Cloud Logging manages logs; it does not run code.

questions.question: Which managed Kubernetes service deploys containerised applications on Google Cloud and can host a secure sandbox for a coding agent?

questions.explanation: Cloud Logging is a real-time log-management system that collects log data from Google Cloud resources automatically.
whyOthersWrong: Cloud Trace tracks request latency rather than managing logs.

Memorystore for Redis is a cache.

Agent Search is a search and recommendation service.

questions.question: An agent calls external tools with 3-legged OAuth, 2-legged OAuth and API keys. Which service is the centralised credentials vault and authentication broker for this?

Firestore is a document database.
Cloud Run runs code.

questions.question: A security team wants to discover, classify and de-identify sensitive data inside and outside Google Cloud. Which service does that?

whyOthersWrong: Agent Gateway governs agent traffic.
Agent Registry catalogues agents, tools and MCP servers.
Cloud Trace tracks request latency.
